title: Sum of Digits
statement: Given a non-negative integer N, print the sum of its digits.
output: One integer: the sum of the digits of N.
hint: Repeatedly take N % 10 to get the last digit, then do N / 10. Use long in Java.

title: Reverse a Number
statement: Given a non-negative integer N, print it with its digits reversed. Leading zeros in the result are dropped (so 1200 becomes 21).
hint: Build the answer as rev = rev * 10 + N % 10 while N > 0.

hint: You only need to try divisors up to √N. Remember 1 is not prime.

title: GCD and LCM
statement: Given two positive integers A and B, print their greatest common divisor and least common multiple.
output: Two integers: GCD and LCM, separated by a space.
hint: Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b). Then lcm = a / gcd * b, which needs long in Java.

title: Second Largest Element
statement: Given an array of N integers, print the second largest distinct value. If it does not exist, print -1.
output: The second largest distinct value, or -1.
hint: One pass: keep first and second. When you see a bigger value, the old first becomes second. Skip values equal to first.

title: Running Sum
statement: Given an array of N integers, print the running (prefix) sum: the i-th output is a[0] + a[1] + … + a[i].
hint: Keep one running total and add each element to it. The total can exceed int, so use long in Java.

title: Rotate Array Right
statement:
Rotate an array of N integers to the right by K steps and print it.

Rotating [1 2 3 4 5] right by 2 gives [4 5 1 2 3].
input: First line N K. Second line N integers.
hint: Rotating by N changes nothing, so use K % N. Element i moves to (i + K) % N.

title: Move Zeros to End
statement: Move all zeros of the array to the end while keeping the order of the non-zero elements, then print the array.
hint: Keep a pointer w for the next write position. Copy each non-zero to a[w++], then fill the rest with zeros.

title: Most Frequent Element
statement: Print the value that appears most often in the array. If several values tie, print the smallest of them.
hint: Count with a HashMap / dict, then scan the counts for the best (value, count) pair.

title: First Unique Character
statement: Given a lowercase string S, print the index (0-based) of the first character that appears exactly once. If none exists, print -1.
hint: First pass: count every letter in an array of 26. Second pass: return the first index whose count is 1.

title: Pair With Target Sum
statement: Is there a pair of different positions i ≠ j with a[i] + a[j] = T? Print YES or NO.
input: First line N T. Second line N integers.
hint: Walk the array once. Before adding x to a set, check whether T − x is already in it.

title: Sort the Array
statement: Print the array in non-decreasing order. Try writing a simple sort yourself first (bubble, selection or insertion), then compare with the built-in sort.
hint: Insertion sort: take each element and shift bigger elements one step right until you find its place.

title: K-th Smallest
statement: Print the K-th smallest element of the array (counting duplicates, 1-based).
input: First line N K. Second line N integers.
hint: Sort, then the answer sits at index K − 1.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
statement: Two arrays are already sorted. Merge them into one sorted array in a single pass, without calling a sort function.
input: Line 1: N. Line 2: N sorted integers. Line 3: M. Line 4: M sorted integers.
hint: Two pointers i and j: always take the smaller of x[i] and y[j], then copy whatever is left.

title: Transpose a Matrix
statement: Print the transpose of an R × C matrix: row i of the answer is column i of the input.
input: First line R C. Next R lines, each with C integers.
hint: Answer cell [j][i] = input cell [i][j]. Loop j on the outside when printing.

title: Diagonal Sum
statement: Given an N × N matrix, print the sum of both diagonals. If N is odd, count the centre cell only once.
input: First line N N. Next N lines, each with N integers.
hint: Main diagonal is [i][i], the other is [i][N−1−i]. Subtract the centre once when N is odd.

title: Spiral Order
statement: Print all cells of an R × C matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting from the top-left.
input: First line R C. Next R lines, each with C integers.
hint: Keep four walls: top, bottom, left, right. Walk one edge, then move that wall inward. Check the walls haven't crossed before the bottom and left edges.
